title: WCAG, POUR & Semantic HTML
objectives: Locate requirements in WCAG and judge conformance levels
Prefer semantic HTML before reaching for ARIA

examples.name: semantics.html
examples.code:
<!-- native semantics: focusable, labelled, announced — zero ARIA -->
<button type="button" @click="save">Save</button>

<label for="email">Email</label>
<input id="email" type="email" required />

<nav aria-label="Main"> ... </nav>

exercise.prompt: Classify each fix under POUR: "add captions to videos" (Perceivable), "make all actions keyboard-reachable" (Operable), "write clear error messages" (Understandable), "use valid ARIA roles the parser understands" (Robust).
hints: Captions make media perceivable; keyboard access makes it operable.

questions.explanation: Native elements bring focus, keyboard activation, and announcement for free.

options: A (minimum) through AA (common target) to AAA (highest)
questions.explanation: AA is the standard legal/production target; AAA is aspirational for parts of a site.
